_source: Watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18 (Professor Of AI, 8.3M views, 2 months old; Hindi, auto-dub available). Frames every 3-6 s plus a 0.4 s burst at 30 s; no sound probe on this one. Shots approximate. Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: split screen: top half real phone footage of a young driver with hands off the wheel; bottom half the presenter pointing at camera; a red label box between them and a small photo inset of a public figure
hook.firstLine: A country's viral 'self-driving car' turns out to be a kid steering with his knees

shots.picture: split screen: viral clip of a driver with hands off the wheel above, presenter talking below, red label and emoji at the seam
full-screen viral phone clip: a young man in the driver's seat steering without hands
presenter at his desk mic asks whether you've ever wondered how real ones work
3D white sedan seen from above, the roof sensor pod highlighted, interior visible
the car camera's view of a building front and fence, what the camera reads
realistic 3D pedestrian walking toward camera on a night street, gesturing
close on the sedan's bumper: yellow radar rings pulse out, a red arrow points at the sensor
top-down: the sedan on a road with yellow pulse rings at each corner sensor, a red car behind
top-down close on the roof: the spinning laser unit, beams implied
the sedan drives a night street, small red markers on its sensors merge
from inside the cockpit: a man in yellow on the road flagged by a red arrow, dashboard text and a mini-map
a lab wall of monitors showing a simulated city with a car driving, a heartbeat-style graph beside it
the sensor car parked in a lit studio garage with a checker floor
back to the lab monitors, a big red arrow bounces over the screen with the real road feed

lines.gist: mocks a country's claim of launching a self-driving car
jokes about the driver honking and turning with his feet, talent galore
asks if you ever wondered how a real one works
it carries a full set of sensors; cameras read lights, signs and text
radar throws out radio waves and works in rain and fog
lidar fires laser beams to build a 3D map; all sensors are fused
software predicts where each person and car will be next second
it was trained first in a fake city inside a computer
only then is it allowed on a real road: a real self-driving car

ending.lastFrame: lab monitor showing the real road feed under a bouncing red arrow

whyItWorks: opens on a viral, mockable clip people already shared, so the first second is recognition plus a joke
the mockery turns into a real how-it-works: each sensor gets its own 3D shot and one visual (rings, beams, text read)
a red bouncing arrow tells the eye exactly where to look in every busy 3D frame
cockpit point-of-view with a flagged pedestrian makes the machine's decision feel personal
